newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firm starts first advanced nuclear reactor.
newsitem.headline: Japan firm starts first advanced nuclear reactor.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc, Japan's biggest power utility, said it started commercial operation of the world's first advanced boiling water reactor (ABWR) on Thursday.
The reactor, located at the utility's Kashiwazaki Kariba nuclear power complex on the sea of Japan coast, has a capacity of 1.35 million kilowatts, a TEPCO spokesman said.
With the new reactor, the Kariba complex becomes the world's second-largest nuclear power complex after a state-owned nuclear power plant in Ontario, Canada, he said.
Japan relies on nuclear power for about 33 percent of its electricity needs and aims to raise dependency to 42 percent by 2010.
The advanced reactor is safer and more economical than the conventional type, the spokesman said.
One of the key features of ABWRs is that the reactor's coolant recirculation pump is installed inside the pressure vessel of the reactor, instead of outside.
Nuclear reactors are safer and easier to operate with coolant piping inside the pressure vessel, TEPCO said.
TEPCO's 16 nuclear reactors, including the new one, have a combined capacity of 15.95 million kilowatts, which accounts for about 30 percent of the utility's power generating facilities.
Construction of the 418 billion yen ($3.73 billion) ABWR started in 1991, and operation began on a trial basis in January this year.
Another ABWR, scheduled to start commercial operation in July 1997, is currently under construction at the Kariba complex.
